verdict.rationale: Both diffs fix December and the same Q4 rollover bug correctly, and both add the same regression tests. B's helper takes a valid month and returns the first day of the following month, so callers never pass an invalid month 13. A's helper relies on that out-of-range sentinel value. B's report also states plainly what was not checked: the tests were not run against the old code, and monthly_report(…, 12) was not called directly. That makes B the slightly better merge.
a_issues: The helper takes an invalid month value (13) as input, which is a slightly awkward contract even though the docstring explains it.
The report says 'The December crash is fixed' but doesn't mention that monthly_report itself was never exercised. Only the range functions are tested.
b_issues: The new helper `_first_of_month_after` has no docstring.
monthly_report(rows, 2026, 12) is not covered by a test, though the report says so.

verdict.rationale: Both diffs fix December and Q4 the same way and add the same two regression tests, so behavior is equivalent. A's helper `_first_of_month_after(year, month)` takes a valid month and returns the next month's start, which reads clearly. B's `_first_of_month` accepts the invalid month 13 as a special case, an odd contract that silently depends on callers never passing other out-of-range values. A's report is also more candid about what was and wasn't verified.
a_issues: No test exercises `monthly_report` or `quarterly_report` for December/Q4 end-to-end, as the report itself acknowledges.
b_issues: Helper `_first_of_month` special-cases month 13, an awkward contract that accepts one invalid month and still raises on others such as 14.
No end-to-end test of `monthly_report(rows, 2026, 12)`, and the report doesn't mention this gap.
